title: White House seeks to limit information contractors should share with Congress
description: The White House is pushing back against congressional oversight as it prepares for expected investigations from a Congress led by Democrats in January.

title: Van Hollen, once an insider, has started Democrats’ first big fight
description: The Maryland Democrat has sought to channel activist anger with Chuck Schumer as he makes an underdog challenge to lead the Senate.

title: The district Alabama remade — and the congressman who held on
description: After the Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act, Rep. Shomari Figures of Alabama and his community carried the mantle of a new civil rights movement.

title: GOP set to block Trump Pentagon picks as other military moves face headwinds
description: Senate Republicans won’t advance two political nominees for key policy jobs. The administration’s nominees to lead the Army and Navy also have encountered resistance, as has its ask for hundreds of billions of dollars in defense funding.

title: Presidential hopefuls start to hint when they might announce their bids
description: Presidential hopefuls tease announcements, governors show off their foreign policy chops, and more.

title: RFK Jr. vows to curb a measles crisis he initially underestimated
description: Federal officials must create a plan to regain measles elimination status. It won’t be easy, public health experts say.

title: How a GOP redistricting 'dummymander' in North Carolina backfired by 2 seats
description: In North Carolina, Republican lawmakers redrew voting maps, aiming to  gain one seat in Congress. Instead, they lost two seats, in a classic example of what political scientists call a "dummymander."

title: The New Yorker's Jason Zengerle on Hakeem Jeffries' rise to first Black House speaker
description: Hakeem Jeffries is set to become the first-ever African American speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives. NPR's Scott Simon talks to Jason Zengerle of The New Yorker about the rise of Jeffries.

title: Week in Politics: Trump returns from Asia; hails trip as one of best in history
description: President Trump returned from his trip to Asia, saying it was one of the most successful presidential visits to that continent -- or anywhere else -- in American history.

title: An effort to circumvent the Electoral College may be within reach. But hurdles remain
description: A national effort to ensure that only winners of the popular vote become president could reach a critical milestone soon.

title: Pentagon watchdog to audit deals with defense tech start-ups
description: It comes after The Washington Post found defense companies tied to President Donald Trump’s sons earned large contracts.

title: In secret memo, Hegseth restricts U.S.-Canada defense relationship
description: The classified directive is another provocation in the Trump administration’s feud with Ottawa. One U.S. official said it’s sure to be seen as a “slap in the face.”

title: Vance declines to say Iran war was worth it, but says he supports Trump
description: Standing next to the president, Vance was asked whether he believed the war was worth Republicans losing the Senate.

title: Trump delights in pomp of Asia trip, with no breakthroughs to report
description: At a news conference, he announced penalties for overseas data centers, an idea he said he didn’t preview to his staff.

title: Texas governor-elect and Trump agree to work together on border security
description: President Donald Trump says he had a “very productive call” with Democratic Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa, who characterized it as “a very positive conversation.”

title: Trump defends Jensen Huang after alleged Chinese spy affair
description: The president said he "would love to see Jensen be given a second chance" at Nvidia.

title: How Americans voted in the midterms, by demographic group and in key states
description: A nationwide survey of voters by NORC examines how different demographic and political groups voted for Congress and in key Senate elections.

title: Another judge blocks Trump’s arch construction in second blow to project
description: The ruling follows a similar decision from a federal judge this week, further ensnaring the president’s plans.

title: California Bar investigating ex-White House press secretary Katie Zacharia
description: Zacharia earned a law degree from Pepperdine University in Southern California and described herself as a lawyer. But she did not pass the bar exam in California, she eventually confirmed.

title: The latest from Trump's press conference
description: President Trump gave a wide-ranging press conference following his historic trip to Asia where he met with Chinese President Xi and Russian President Putin.

title: White House replaces top cybersecurity official after string of outages
description: The departure of Sean Cairncross continues the ouster of aides associated with former chief of staff Susie Wiles.

title: Agriculture secretary’s ‘proselytizing’ emails are unconstitutional, judge rules
description: Emails that Brooke Rollins sent to USDA staff about Christmas and Easter also breached the department’s own rules, the judge said.

title: A second judge blocks Trump's arch, saying it's unlikely to succeed in court
description: A federal judge in Virginia said she will issue a preliminary injunction against Trump's arch, going a step further than the D.C. federal judge who temporarily blocked construction earlier this week.

title: Trump initially accepted the midterm results, but most GOP voters doubt they were fair
description: Less than half of Republicans nationwide considered the midterm elections "free and fair," according to new polling.

title: A young Kennedy joined the Kennedy Center fight, on the outside looking in
description: JFK’s 22-year-old great-niece is working behind the scenes at the law firm challenging Trump’s attempted overhaul. Her first visit came just after the center closed.

title: Americans voted for Democratic leaders — that doesn’t mean they like them
description: “Many of the folks who voted for us yesterday, of course, are still skeptical,” Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer acknowledged the day after the election.

title: Trump touts meeting with Xi and Putin but offers few results
description: At a White House press conference Friday, Trump offered little in actual results of the meetings, beyond a joint statement on unity over some issues.

title: Democratic stars try to keep 2028 spotlight as newbies surge after midterms
description: Some Democratic presidential hopefuls who planned to launch their campaigns shortly after the midterms changed their plans after the unexpectedly large wins.

title: Democrats aim to intensify the focus on Nvidia in new Congress
description: Lawmakers are seeking to learn more about the Trump administration’s relationship with the chipmaker and whether top officials stood to profit from a known export loophole.

title: Top Democrat asks Trump administration to stop using disappearing messaging apps
description: Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Maryland), who is poised to lead the House Judiciary Committee, sent letters to federal law enforcement agencies.

title: Texas execution took over an hour as staff struggled to find vein; Reinaldo Dennes moaned about pain
description: The same day Dennes was given lethal injection, Florida carried out a record-breaking 20th execution of the year.

title: Dems aim to block Iran war funding. And, Army delays lead azide detonation in Iowa
description: Congress needs to pass a funding measure to avoid a shutdown next month, providing Dems an opportunity to leverage power. And, the Army says waiting to detonate lead azide could become dangerous.

title: These are the Senate Democrats backing Schumer and Van Hollen for majority leader
description: The Post is tracking senators’ public comments on the fight for Senate majority leader in the next Congress.

title: Justice Dept. drops appeal in bid to delay certification of Alaska Senate win
description: The DOJ said that since ballots had been counted, it was impossible to carry out the type of investigation it had sought.

title: A child support fight exposed a Trump adviser’s $15 million income
description: Jason Miller’s income rose sharply after Trump’s return to power, court records show. The longtime aide’s firms kept receiving payments after he began appearing more regularly at the White House.

title: President Trump pardons disgraced MLB star Pete Rose, who died in 2024
description: Trump has been vocal about wanting to see Rose in the Baseball Hall of Fame. This likely won't help.

title: The one thing Putin, Trump and Xi agreed on — fewer limits on major powers
description: In a joint statement, the three leaders said they would work to reform the United Nations, limit the International Criminal Court and reduce energy sanctions.

title: Iran war has worsened U.S. munitions shortage, government watchdog finds
description: A Government Accountability Office report contradicts assertions made by President Donald Trump and other administration officials who have rejected stockpile concerns.

title: Senate rejects resolution to block Trump from striking Iran
description: The vote was the first test of Republican support for the war since they lost control of Congress in the midterms.

title: DOJ sends top L.A. prosecutor to work on Florida grand conspiracy case
description: Bill Essayli’s role will focus on the Biden administration’s investigation into Trump’s allegedly improper retention of sensitive government materials after his first term.

title: Boise students accused of sending violent texts citing Cornell case sue schools
description: The high school football players filed a lawsuit against the Idaho district over their suspension.

title: White House largely mum in aftermath of historic three-way summit
description: Trump schedules a news conference for Friday but has little to say in the immediate aftermath of an historic trilateral meeting.

title: Buttigieg supporters launch group to support a presidential bid
description: Ex-aides to the former transportation secretary organized the Team Pete PAC to build a grassroots network and encourage a 2028 campaign.

title: Arts panel asks Trump administration to rethink East Potomac golf course’s scope
description: The panel of Trump appointees appeared skeptical of the administration’s plan to cut off access to East Potomac Park to build a championship course.

title: Democrats renew push for records from law firms that struck deals with Trump
description: The investigative pressure comes as Democrats are set to take control of the House and the Senate in January, after decisive victories in the midterm elections.

title: Absent Republicans are a problem for House leaders in the lame-duck session
description: While addressing reporters Thursday, House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-Louisiana) lamented missed votes by members of his party.

title: Proposed change to SNAP threatens free school meals for 1.7 million children
description: A Trump administration proposal affecting automatic enrollment could cut benefits for millions of families.

title: Tracking who Trump is appointing to fill key administration roles
description: Follow President Trump’s progress filling over 800 positions, among about 1,300 that require Senate confirmation, in this tracker from The Washington Post and the Partnership for Public Service.

title: Are Republican voters still loyal to Trump? What new polls say.
description: Plus: How polls actually work with caller ID.
